source.title: Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting for Random Orthogonal Transformation Tasks in the Overparameterized Regime

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model size and reports generalization risk in a linear regression setting, testing the overparameterized declining part of the size-wise claim with a different model and task setup.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses and cites double descent, but cited results are not extracted as findings of this study. Its own MNIST experiment compares accuracy at different widths; it does not locate an interpolation threshold or report a full double-descent curve. No epoch-wise or sample-size sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: The paper is about catastrophic forgetting. Its only own result on the claim is the single-task risk R(fβ̂A) of a min-norm linear estimator, plotted against p for p>n (Fig. 3); the text says it is decreasing in the overparameterized regime. This bears weakly on the post-interpolation descent in V4 for a non-deep model class. No peak, underparameterized regime, epoch or sample sweep is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also note the overparameterization needed is only linear in n, and give a geometric explanation: overparameterization makes the tasks live in near-orthogonal subspaces.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes sequential task learning with random orthogonal transformations and measures task risk or forgetting as p varies; it does not reproduce the original double-descent measurement of test error across the interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: Risk decreases with p in the reported overparameterized sweep; the numerical experiment fixes γ=1. The theorem’s bound also depends on γ.

fits_no_version.finding: In 10-task permuted MNIST, wider MLPs trained with vanilla SGD retain more average accuracy across tasks, recovering much of the gain from SI/EWC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization mitigates catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-A risk after sequential training on an orthogonally transformed task B decreases with p. The risk gap to single-task training is bounded by (66√(n/p)+12/(pγ))‖θ‖² with high probability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In linear two-task regression related by random orthogonal transforms, the forgetting risk gap shrinks as the overparameterization ratio p/n grows.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The size-wise numerical risk results are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The MNIST evidence is an endpoint width comparison and does not establish an interpolation threshold or a full double-descent curve. The theoretical result is for a specific linear model with random orthogonal task transformations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out.

untested.parts: Not tested: no single-task test error versus width in deep networks, and no interpolation threshold or peak.

Not tested: the underparameterized regime (p<n), the peak near p=n, and the comparison of the second descent with the classical U-curve. Only the p>n descent in one noiseless-response linear latent model is shown.

record.verdict_notes: The study's link to double descent is mostly motivational: it cites Nakkiran et al. and Belkin et al. and adopts a linear model known to show monotone overparameterized risk. The V4 evidence is a single figure-only curve restricted to p>n, with no peak shown. The reader's V1 support label is dropped because r1 measures continual-learning forgetting, not model-wise test error. Appendix C (Fig. 4) repeats the curves with permutation tasks and gives the same qualitative behaviour.

versions.untested_parts: The full fall-rise-fall curve and the location of a peak near the interpolation threshold are not tested; the reported width comparison is limited to w=1 and w=9.
The underparameterized regime and a peak near interpolation are not tested; results cover the overparameterized regime of one linear model setup.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP trained with Vanilla SGD
rows.operation_detail: Compared test accuracy at different layer widths during sequential learning.
rows.measure: Average test accuracy on all seen tasks
rows.value: w=9; numerical value figure only; text reports that overparameterization obtains a significant fraction of the accuracy gain achieved by SI or EWC
rows.note: The text reports a comparison of w=1 and w=9, not a full width-wise curve or the interpolation threshold. Accuracy is the reported measure.
rows.check: The measure is average accuracy on all seen tasks after sequential 10-task permuted-MNIST training, which measures forgetting, not single-task test error versus size. Widths w=1–9 ([400w,400w]) are not placed relative to an interpolation threshold, and values are figure-only. It does not bear on V1.

relationships.display_finding: Single-task prediction risk decreased with p throughout the tested overparameterized regime.
